proposal_set.name: prefill-chunk-budget-4096
proposal_set.reason: Largest measured loss is mixed prefill+decode steps: steady decode hits gt~729 tok/s only in pure-decode windows (10:37:44-10:51:24), but from 10:53 onward every 10s window mixes prefill (pt 750-1400 tok/s) with decode and generation collapses to 100-280 tok/s. With ISL=1024 at the default budget of 2048, the scheduler fits 2 prompts per step, so ~44% of steps (100/310 windows had Running<64) are mixed and GDN+attention run at two different shapes per step. Raising the budget to 4096 lets 4 full prompts per step and, on the ~1400-1650 tok/s prefill streams, returns whole steps to pure decode. Capacity is not binding (KV peaks 58.5%, 294,473 tokens) and 8GiB of KV headroom was unclaimed at gpu-memory-utilization=0.95, so a larger step is affordable.

proposal_set.name: gdn-ssm-state-bf16
proposal_set.reason: 48 of 64 layers are GDN and their recurrent state is fp32 only because the checkpoint declares mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and vLLM auto-adopts it - not because a kernel requires fp32. At conc=64 that state store is the largest per-step HBM traffic source, so halving it attacks decode directly, and it also halves the mamba page that currently forces attention block_size up to 784 tokens. Verified in the LIVE tree that bf16 is a first-class choice and stays on the fused paths: MambaDType includes 'bfloat16' (config/cache.py:38) and FUSED_GDN_STATE_DTYPES=(float32,bfloat16), so fp16 would fall off the whitelist while bf16 does not. Held to rank 3 only because the accuracy gate, not throughput, is the binding risk on a W8A8 checkpoint at 0.9674.

proposal_set.name: no-prefix-cache-packed-decode
proposal_set.reason: ATOMIC: both halves are required. With prefix caching on, mamba cache mode is forced to 'align', which only snapshots the state of the last token of each scheduler step and makes the per-step CoW/page-identity bookkeeping run on every mixed step. The packed FLA recurrent-decode fast path (env default is already 1) fires ONLY when attn_metadata.num_prefills == 0 - so it never engages during the mixed steps that cost 100-280 gt/s, and it cannot engage while 'align' retains per-step state. Turning prefix caching off flips mode to 'none', drops the align bookkeeping and lets whole pure-decode steps take the packed path. Flagged as the speculative pick: it trades away a 75.4% prefix-cache hit rate, which the same log shows is doing real work, so the net can easily be negative. NOTE: unset_envs AITER_LOG_TUNED_CONFIG is hygiene only (hint #6 calls it pure log noise), not a third coupled half; drop it if you want a cleaner A/B attribution.

new_findings.what: The prefill-stall model in the scout hint is coarsely right but mechanically different, and the difference changes which lever helps. There is NO window with Running=64 and near-zero generation (min gt at R=64 is 80.4). The losses are (a) batch-turnover windows where Running collapses (R=0,W=0 engine drain 10:51:34-44 plus a 90s stats gap to 10:53:14) and (b) sustained MIXED prefill+decode steps from 10:53 onward at pt 750-1400 / gt 100-280. Prefill stream plateaued at ~1843 tok/s (2 prompts/step at the 2048 default). So this is a step-composition problem, not a starvation problem: batch-budget and decode-path-unity levers are on the hot path, capacity levers are not.
new_findings.expected_impact: re-ranks the candidate set: prefill-chunk-budget moves above the dtype change on risk-adjusted value

new_findings.what: AITER is falling back to default GEMM solutions for exactly the shapes this workload produces. The log records a8w8 INT8 ScaledMM at M:784 (N:16384/34816/17408/14336/5120) and M:1568/1667/1697 with 'not found tuned config in a8w8_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config'. M:784 is the mamba-derived attention block size, and 1568 = 2x784. On gfx90a get_cdna_version()==2 makes is_aiter_found_and_supported() False, so the AITER tuning bridges stay dead and no env switch here will help. A config-only nudge is --mamba-block-size (exists at engine/arg_utils.py:1240), but it collides with prefix caching because block_size 784 exists precisely to make the mamba and attention page sizes equal, so it is a patch-scale decision, not a flag.

new_findings.expected_impact: 1-5% if tuned shapes can be steered without breaking page-size equality; needs kernel/patch ownership
